question: Should OpenClaw preserve the documented, release-reachable manual-action response fields at the Gateway/CLI boundary while adopting the closed internal state, or intentionally make this a breaking contract change now?
rationale: The branch correctly identifies that this is not process-local state: published plugin Gateway results and user documentation expose the legacy field names, so choosing a compatibility window versus a projection is an API policy decision.

options.title: Add boundary compatibility
options.body: Keep `manualAction` as the canonical internal representation and project the three legacy fields only at supported Gateway/CLI response boundaries with regression coverage.

options.title: Approve a breaking window
options.body: Accept removal of the legacy fields only with an explicit maintainer-approved API contract window and clear upgrade communication.

options.title: Defer the refactor
options.body: Pause the public response-shape change until a broader meeting API versioning or deprecation plan is agreed.

recommendation.title: Add boundary compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep `manualAction` as the canonical internal representation and project the three legacy fields only at supported Gateway/CLI response boundaries with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR body already identifies the public-contract discovery and presents the concrete compatibility choices.
